name: Phragmites

look_here_first: COMMON REED: robust very tall jointed perennial stems, long broad leaves, underground rhizomes and enormous silver-tan feathery panicles. CRITICAL: Phragmites australis includes native North American and invasive introduced lineages. Do not identify lineage from this single photo or decide on treatment without native/introduced subspecies evaluation.

comparison_lesson.title: Common reed comparison
comparison_lesson.memory_rule: COMMON REED: robust very tall jointed perennial stems, long broad leaves, underground rhizomes and enormous silver-tan feathery panicles. CRITICAL: Phragmites australis includes native North American and invasive introduced lineages. Do not identify lineage from this single photo or decide on treatment without native/introduced subspecies evaluation.
quick_split: Arundo donax (giant reed) has bamboo-like robust stems, frequently wide leaves and different denser seedhead spikelets; Zizaniopsis miliacea (giant cutgrass) is another tall native wetland grass with a more open panicle and different spikelets. To distinguish Phragmites native vs introduced, compare multi-character sheath, leaf, culm and glume traits and ideally genetics/provenance; never a single seedhead.
comparison_lesson.guardrail: Species-level image CANNOT support an introduced/invasive claim: native subspecies and introduced lineages overlap in morphology.
